name: pet-offers
description: The pet notices an error or failure with plain local rules, offers help in a bubble, and acts only after a tap. This file is the one source for every surface: offer shape, kinds, copy, rules, block defaults, settings and test fixtures. Generated copies come from generate.mjs; never edit them by hand.

id.note: Random id, unique per offer on the device.

app.note: Display name of the app the error came from, e.g. Terminal. Used for {App} in copy.

appId.note: Bundle id (mac/iOS), exe name (Windows), package (Android), or 'allternit' for own failures.

windowKey.note: appId + '|' + title. Gate key: one offer per windowKey per cooldownMs, and never the same trigger.line twice for one windowKey.

ruleId.note: Id of the rule that matched, or 'event' for a failure event that needs no text rule (run_failed).

line.note: The matched line, trimmed, at most limits.lineMaxChars characters.

text.note: The read text (tail-biased, at most maxTextChars). Stays in memory on the device until the user accepts. Never put it in a notification, a log or a URL query string.

botId.note: The bot whose pet makes the offer.

kindNotes.error_dialog: An app shows an error or crash dialog.
kindNotes.stack_trace: A command or program printed an error or stack trace.
kindNotes.build_failed: A build, compile or test run failed.
kindNotes.run_failed: An Allternit bot run or turn failed. Comes from the app's own failure event, not from a text rule (ruleId 'event').

byKind.stack_trace: That command hit an error. Fix it?
byKind.error_dialog: {App} is showing an error. Fix it?

notification.title: Allternit
notification.body: Your bot spotted an error. Fix it?

copy.placeholderNote: Replace {App} with the offer's app display name, or appFallback when the name is empty.
copy.notificationNote: Notifications (Android heads-up, lock screen) always use notification.body. Never screen text, never the app name.

steps: If the text is longer than maxTextChars, keep only the last maxTextChars characters.
Walk rules in file order. Skip a rule whose scope is 'dialog' unless the text came from a window or element with a dialog role (see dialogRoles).
The first rule whose pattern finds a match wins. Result: {kind, ruleId, line}, where line is the whole line holding the start of the match, trimmed, cut to limits.lineMaxChars.
matcher.regexDialect: Portable subset of JS RegExp, ICU (NSRegularExpression) and java.util.regex: no lookbehind, no named groups or backreferences, no inline flags, no \p{...}, no atomic or possessive groups, no \A \Z \z, ASCII only (write \u2019 for a curly apostrophe). Flags are only 'i' (case-insensitive) and 'm' (^ and $ match at line breaks). '.' never matches a newline.

rules.pattern: (The application was unable to start correctly|is not a valid Win32 application|The program can['\u2019]t start because|\bhas stopped working\b)
FAILURE: Build failed with an exception
\b(error|failed|failure|couldn['\u2019]t|could not|cannot be opened|can['\u2019]t be opened|unexpectedly|crashed|not responding)\b

dialogRoles.note: A text read counts as 'dialog' when its window or a parent element has one of these roles or classes. Only then do scope 'dialog' rules apply.

block.order: Check before any read: app block list (password managers, banking, messages, user blockList), then window context (title and URL), then private-window and banking-host checks, then read the text. A browser whose title cannot be read is not read.

passwordManagers.match: Block when the app display name equals a name (case-insensitive) or the appId equals an appId. Names win when an id is unknown or missing.

banking.match: Name: a keyword appears as whole words in the app name or window title (case-insensitive). Host: the URL host equals a suffix or ends with '.' + suffix, or any dot-separated host label contains a hostLabelKeyword.

privateWindowTitles.match: Case-insensitive substring of the window title. A match means the window is not read.

neverRead.note: Never read secure text fields: AXSecureTextField (mac), UIA IsPassword=true (Windows), AccessibilityNodeInfo.isPassword() (Android). Skip the element and its value entirely; do not keep a placeholder or length.

notes.petOffers.enabled: Offers for Allternit's own failures and terminal hook signals. On by default.
notes.petOffers.readOtherApps: EOJ SWITCH. The single default for reading other apps' windows on Desktop. false = off until the user turns it on from the one-time pet bubble or Settings (macOS only allows the Accessibility prompt from a user action). Flip this one value and rerun generate.mjs to change it everywhere.
notes.petOffers.cooldownMs: One offer per windowKey per this many ms.
notes.petOffers.bubbleMs: How long the offer bubble stays up.
notes.petOffers.tailChars: Last characters kept from the largest text element.
notes.petOffers.blockList: User-added app ids or names never read. Adds to block defaults; never replaces them.
notes.petOffers.muted: App ids the user muted with 'Mute {App}'. Still read for nothing: muted apps are skipped before any read.

settings.storage: Device-local only: electron-store (Desktop), localStorage (web/phone/PWA), UserDefaults (iOS), SharedPreferences (Android), gizzi pet settings file (Gizzi). No server sync.

computer.meaning: true turns on the computer tools for this one turn only. Set when the user picks 'computer tools on' while accepting a Desktop offer.
computer.flow: renderer send options -> metadata.tools on the turn -> stored_turn_metadata (allternit-api v1_routes.rs, forwarded whole) -> gizzi runtime MobileTools.
computer.persistence: None. Not stored on the session, no migration.
computer.olderRuntimes: Ignore the key; the turn runs without computer tools.
computer.controlLease: Not taken automatically. The first mouse or keyboard step shows the existing take-control prompt.
computer.safety: The computer_safety.rs confirm gate (money, send, delete) still applies.
